title: Applying Payments and Refunds to Window Contracts
content:
# Applying Payments and Refunds to Window Contracts

Billing office note for Window Replacement Contracts.

**Rule.** Every payment is applied to exactly one contract and is never split across contracts. The payment goes to the contract whose contract number the customer gives; when the customer names no contract and holds more than one open window replacement contract, it goes to the open contract with the earliest signed date that still has a balance due, and to the next one only once a new payment is made. Lender funding is applied to the contract named on the funded financing account. A refund is always booked against the same contract as the payment it returns and names that payment as its source. It never draws on a payment recorded on another contract.

An open window replacement contract is one in status signed, measured, ordered or installed.

## Where a payment goes

| Situation | Contract the payment is applied to |
|---|---|
| The customer gives a contract number | That contract |
| No contract named; the customer holds more than one open window contract | The open contract with the earliest signed date that still has a balance due |
| Lender funding | The contract named on the funded financing account |

A payment is never divided between two contracts. When the earliest-signed open contract with a balance due is fully paid, the next payment, not the remainder of the same payment, goes to the next one.

## Refund binding

A refund is booked on the same contract as the payment it returns and names that payment as its source; the system records of the payment and its contract decide this, and a refund never draws on a payment recorded on another contract.

## Hypothetical case

A customer holds two open window contracts signed on hypothetical dates in March 2031 and May 2031, each with a balance due, and pays without naming a contract. The payment goes in full to the contract signed in March 2031.
